high.title: Natura (NATU3) leads Ibovespa gains and RD Saúde (RADL3) is worst performing stock; see weekly highlights
high.summary: The Ibovespa completed its second consecutive week of gains, rising 3.58% to close at 188,042.02 points amid uncertainties about the Iran conflict duration and Brazil's electoral scenario. The USD/BRL fell 1.56% during the week, closing at R$ 5.1599, showing BRL strength. Central Bank President Gabriel Galípolo explained that the monetary authority opted for a smaller interest rate cut to "gain more time" for assessment. In March, COPOM reduced the Selic rate from 15% to 14.75% per annum. Galípolo stated that "the cushion accumulated with a more conservative position allowed gaining time to better understand the scenario and continue with the planned trajectory." This dovish commentary suggests the BCB remains cautious about further aggressive cuts. The market continues focusing on Middle East conflict implications for monetary policy, while the first electoral polls are drawing attention to Brazil's political landscape.

medium.title: 10 stocks to invest and outperform Ibovespa in April, according to Safra
medium.summary: Safra adjusted its recommended stock portfolio for April, replacing Allos (ALOS3) with Multiplan (MULT3) and rebalancing weights among assets. The bank reduced Bradesco (BBDC4) exposure due to marginal deterioration in the domestic banking environment, particularly in credit segments amid increased judicial recovery requests. Vale (VALE3) exposure was increased after recent weak performance, while Multiplan entered following underperformance that created attractive valuation opportunities.

medium.title: Dividends: Itaú BBA replaces Aura Minerals (AURA33) with Petrobras (PETR4) in April; see stocks
medium.summary: Itaú BBA modified its dividend portfolio for April, removing Aura Minerals (AURA33) and adding Petrobras (PETR4). The bank expects Petrobras to benefit from higher oil prices through upward diesel price adjustments, projecting generous dividend distributions. In March, the dividend portfolio fell 6.5%, underperforming Ibovespa by 5.8 percentage points, with Bradesco's 9% decline being the main negative contributor due to weak banking sector performance.
